description: TinyClaw - Tiny memory infrastructure for AgentHLE, inspired by OpenClaw's memory system. Plain markdown files, task-scoped cross-session memory, keyword + hybrid semantic search, agent-driven memory writing, periodic reflection callbacks, and LLM post-hoc compaction. See docs/memory-system.md for full design and docs/testing-feedback-loops.md for verification guidelines.

userStories.title: Wire all memory tools into agent and clean up scaffolding
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all memory tools (search, get, write) wired into the agent with proper instructions, and the existing scaffolding code removed. This is the single story that modifies agenthle_agent.py for the memory tool suite.

context.currentState: Agent currently has: (1) MemoryStore init + MemorySearchTool wired in, (2) step counter logging to daily log (lines 112-115, anti-pattern), (3) post-run self-verification code (lines 154-171, anti-pattern)

acceptanceCriteria: Remove step counter logging (lines 112-115: 'Step N: tokens=X' appended every turn — anti-pattern)
Remove post-run self-verification code (lines 154-171: memory_search call + log evidence — test scaffolding in production code)
MemoryStore initialized with task_id from task config (derived from task directory name or config tag)
MemoryStore.init_session() called at start to create session file
TASK_MEMORY.md content injected into agent instructions at session start (if exists)
All three tools wired into ComputerAgent tools= list: MemorySearchTool, MemoryGetTool, MemoryWriteTool
Agent instructions updated to describe all three tools and when to use each

Level 2: After a real run, trajectory logs show agent invoked at least one memory tool autonomously
Level 2: Memory files contain task-relevant content (not just step counters)
Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
userStories.notes:
This is the integration story that wires everything together. All tool stories (MEM-003, W01) and storage (TSK-S) must be done first. After this story, the agent has a complete memory tool suite and clean production code.

CRITICAL DESIGN INSIGHT (see docs/cua-context-management.md): The CUA agent's context is a narrow sliding window. ImageRetentionCallback keeps only the last N screenshot triplets (reasoning + computer_call + computer_call_output), and OpenAI's truncation:auto drops the rest. By turn 100, only ~20 items survive out of ~300+. This has two key implications:

1. TASK_MEMORY.md MUST be injected into the `instructions` parameter (not as a tool result), because PromptInstructionsCallback prepends it on EVERY turn — it's the only content guaranteed to never be truncated. This is the primary cross-session knowledge transfer mechanism.

2. function_call_output items (memory_search/memory_get results) are ephemeral — they get truncated by the API like everything else. The agent only benefits from search results in the turn they're retrieved. Don't rely on the agent choosing to search; the most important memory goes in instructions.

userStories.notes:
Currently the computer-use agent performs summarization via the nudge prompt. Later replaceable by a planner LLM (gpt-5-mini via MEMORY_COMPACTION_MODEL). See docs/memory-system.md for design.

Implementation note: The nudge should be injected via on_llm_start (appending a user message to the message list), similar to how PromptInstructionsCallback prepends instructions. This ensures the nudge is visible in the current turn's context. See docs/cua-context-management.md for how the CUA context window works and why on_llm_start is the correct hook.

userStories.title: Improved memory recall prompting strategy
userStories.description: As an agent, I want clearer, task-agnostic instructions about when and how to use memory_search so I actually invoke it at the right moments instead of forgetting it exists.

context.reference: OpenClaw system-prompt.ts buildMemorySection() — uses task-agnostic categorical triggers (prior work, decisions, dates, strategies, mistakes) not task-specific ones

acceptanceCriteria: Agent instructions contain a dedicated '## Memory Recall' section (not buried in general instructions)

Memory recall section lists task-agnostic trigger categories (e.g., prior observations, past strategies, known mistakes, previous decisions — NOT game-specific like 'floor numbers' or 'enemy encounters')

Level 1: Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
Level 1: Smoke test run_magic_tower.sh --max-steps 5 doesn't crash

Level 2: After run_magic_tower.sh (step count at discretion), trajectory logs (turn_NNN/NNNN_agent_response.json) show agent invoked memory_search in at least 3 distinct decision-making contexts (not just once at start). Use: grep -r '"memory_search"' trajectories/
Level 2: Agent reasoning summaries (response.output[].summary[].text) after memory_search calls reference the retrieved content
Level 2: Search queries in trajectory logs are task-relevant (not random or empty strings)
userStories.notes:
Future story. Inspired by OpenClaw's system prompt design (buildMemorySection in system-prompt.ts). The current TinyClaw instructions are too vague — 'before making decisions' doesn't give the model enough signal to actually trigger recall. OpenClaw's categorical triggers (prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, todos) are more effective. This story adapts that pattern with task-agnostic categories that work across all CUA tasks, not just games. The exact prompt wording should be determined during implementation. See docs/memory-system.md 'Memory Recall' section for full analysis.

Optional enhancement (not required for this story): session-start auto-search — programmatically call memory_search with task-relevant keywords before the first agent step, so prior context is pre-loaded into the conversation.
